models_evaluated: Single vendor portfolio of 13 radiology AI models for 12 clinical tasks

links.outcome: Augmentation metrics (AI-detected radiologist-missed cases) predicting postdeployment perceived value
links.effect: Absolute and relative enhanced detection rates ranged 0.03-2.27% and 4.5-60.5%; predicted value categories agreed with postdeployment radiologist survey for 10 of 12 tasks (response rate 43.2%, 54/125).
links.quote: Perceived value categories agreed between survey respondents and workgroup predictions for 10 of 12 tasks.

links.outcome: Predeployment comparison of AI versus radiologist performance on the same examinations
links.effect: Radiologists generally had higher PPV, AI higher sensitivity; the combined predeployment evaluation showed high agreement with real-world postdeployment value perceptions (10 of 12 tasks).
links.quote: A validation survey indicated high agreement between predeployment predictions and real-world postdeployment value perceptions.

unlisted_practices: Structured weighting of task-inherent value attributes (tediousness, miss likelihood, clinical impact of miss) to predict AI value before purchase

models_evaluated: 13 AI models from a single unnamed vendor for 12 clinical tasks

links.outcome: AI versus radiologist positive predictive value and sensitivity
links.effect: Radiologists generally had higher PPV, whereas AI generally had higher sensitivity; neither consistently outperformed the other across both metrics.
links.quote: Across tasks, radiologists generally had higher PPV, whereas AI generally had higher sensitivity.

links.outcome: Agreement between locally informed predeployment value predictions and postdeployment perceived value
links.effect: Predictions combining task-inherent value with local radiologist and AI performance agreed with postdeployment perceived value for 10 of 12 tasks. Survey response rate was 43.2% (54/125).
links.quote: Perceived value categories agreed between survey respondents and workgroup predictions for 10 of 12 tasks.
